events.title: Notion all-in-one workspace launches
events.summary: Notion released its first public tools in June 2016 — blending notes, wikis, databases, and task boards in one block-based editor.
events.about: Notion let startups replace Confluence, Trello, and Google Docs with linked pages and [relational database]s — `/code` blocks, templates, and team wikis in a single app. It became the default knowledge base for indie hackers and product teams who wanted flexible docs without Atlassian licensing.

narrative.whyChosen: Notion unified docs, tasks, and lightweight databases for modern teams.
narrative.whyImportant: Block-based pages made internal wikis approachable for non-engineers.
narrative.problemSolved: Teams juggled separate tools for notes, specs, and project tracking.

events.title: Windows Subsystem for Linux released
events.summary: Microsoft shipped Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL) in the Windows 10 Anniversary Update on August 2, 2016 — running Linux ELF binaries on Windows without a VM.
events.about: WSL let developers run bash, apt, and Node tooling on Windows laptops — `wsl` became standard in full-stack setup guides. WSL 2 later added a real Linux [kernel], blurring the line between Windows and Linux dev environments.

narrative.whyChosen: WSL brought native Linux tooling to Windows developers.
narrative.whyImportant: It reduced friction for cross-platform and open-source workflows on Windows.
narrative.problemSolved: Windows developers dual-booted or ran slow VMs to use Linux build chains.

events.title: PowerShell open-sourced on GitHub
events.summary: Microsoft open-sourced PowerShell on August 18, 2016 and announced PowerShell on Linux and macOS — porting the Windows shell to cross-platform infrastructure automation.
events.about: PowerShell Core replaced Windows-only shell scripting for DevOps teams running heterogeneous clouds: same cmdlets for Azure, AWS, and on-prem Windows/Linux. It became the backbone of modern Windows automation alongside Bash on Linux servers.

narrative.whyChosen: Open PowerShell was Microsoft's bid to own cross-platform automation, not just Windows admin.
narrative.whyImportant: It let operators use one object pipeline language across [OS] boundaries.
narrative.problemSolved: Cloud-era teams managed Linux and Windows hosts but lacked a unified automation shell.

events.title: Samsung Galaxy Note 7 released
events.summary: Samsung released the Samsung Galaxy Note 7 — iris scanner and curved display — recalled worldwide for battery defects.
events.about: The Galaxy Note targeted stylus power users on [Android]. Iris scanner and curved display — recalled worldwide for battery defects. Note apps and split-screen [Android] development often targeted this hardware class.

narrative.whyChosen: The Samsung Galaxy Note 7 advanced Samsung's stylus phablet line.
narrative.whyImportant: Galaxy Note hardware defined large-screen [Android] productivity for years.
narrative.problemSolved: [Android] lacked a premium large-screen stylus flagship for note-taking workflows.
